Blosc2 cd_values Reference

Source: vignettes/articles/blosc2-cd-values.Rmd
blosc2-cd-values.Rmd

Most code should add the Blosc2 filter with hdf5lib_set_blosc2(), which builds its parameters for you; see Compression & Filters. This page sets out those parameters, the filter’s cd_values, for the rare cases that need them: calling H5Pset_filter() yourself, or reading the list H5Pget_filter_by_id() returns for a dataset.

The plugin’s cd_values follow the layout of the reference HDF5-Blosc2 filter (the one hdf5plugin, PyTables and The HDF Group build) slot for slot, so other implementations can read, describe and append to hdf5lib’s datasets. The reference has room for a single pre-filter and no codec parameters, so the plugin packs the rest of its settings, the whole pre-filter pipeline and one parameter byte, into cd_values[0], which the reference only uses for its revision number and never reads.

The layout

  • Filter ID: 32026
  • Elements (cd_nelmts): 7
Slot You pass The plugin stores
cd_values[0] The packed settings below The same, less anything that does not run (see below)
cd_values[1] 0 0: Blosc2 picks the block size
cd_values[2] 0 The item size in bytes
cd_values[3] 0 The chunk size in bytes
cd_values[4] Compression level, 0 to 9 The same, or 255 for a dataset a ZFP codec cannot take
cd_values[5] 0, or the code of the last pre-filter The code of the last pre-filter
cd_values[6] Codec The same
cd_values[7], [8...] Nothing The chunk rank and shape, for chunks compressed as B2ND arrays

The packed settings in cd_values[0]:

Bits Contents
31-24 0xB2, marking the value as hdf5lib’s
23-20 Layout version, 1
19-16 Pre-filter bitmask
15-8 Meta value
7-0 1, the reference filter’s revision

That is, cd_values[0] = 0xB2100001 + (bitmask << 16) + (meta << 8), where the bitmask and meta value are hdf5lib_set_blosc2()’s prefilters and meta. The bitmask is the sum of 1 (shuffle), 2 (bitshuffle), 4 (delta) and 8 (trunc-prec), the values of HDF5LIB_BLOSC2_SHUFFLE and the rest. A negative meta value goes in as its 8-bit equivalent, 256 + meta: -3 is 253 (0xFD). Compression & Filters explains what each pre-filter and meta value does.

  • cd_values[4]: Compression level (0 to 9). A higher level makes H5Dcreate2() fail; the plugin itself records 255 for a dataset a ZFP codec cannot take, so that every chunk is stored unfiltered.
  • cd_values[5]: the last pre-filter that runs, as a single Blosc2 filter code, which is what the reference filter keeps in this slot: 2 if the bitmask has bitshuffle, else 1 if shuffle, else 3 if delta, else 4 if trunc-prec, else 0. The plugin works it out from the bitmask, so pass 0 or that code; any other value makes H5Dcreate2() fail with a message naming the code expected.
  • cd_values[6]: the codec, as hdf5lib_set_blosc2()’s codec (0=blosclz, 1=lz4, 2=lz4hc, 4=zlib, 5=zstd, 32=ndlz, 33=zfp_acc, 34=zfp_prec, 35=zfp_rate).

The list the plugin stores records only what runs, so it may differ from the one you passed. The ZFP codecs and NDLZ skip the pre-filters, so their bitmask and cd_values[5] are stored as 0. With bitshuffle, the shuffle bit is dropped; truncate-precision is dropped on data it cannot take, or when it would keep every bit. The meta value is stored as 0 when nothing reads it, and NDLZ’s as 4 or 8. For chunks of 2 to 16 dimensions the plugin adds the rank and shape in cd_values[7] onwards, as the reference does, except for array datatypes, which it compresses as plain Blosc2, and ZFP chunks of more than 4 dimensions or with a dimension under 4, which it compresses as one long row. NDLZ always records the 2-D byte image it compresses. Values you pass after cd_values[6] are ignored.

Example

Truncating floats to 16 bits of precision, applying Bitshuffle, and compressing with LZ4 at level 5, which hdf5lib_set_blosc2() sets up as:

hdf5lib_set_blosc2(plist_id, H5Z_FLAG_MANDATORY, HDF5LIB_BLOSC2_LZ4, 5,
                   HDF5LIB_BLOSC2_TRUNC_PREC | HDF5LIB_BLOSC2_BITSHUFFLE, 16);

The same, passed to H5Pset_filter() directly:

// cd_values[0]: bitmask Truncprec (8) + Bitshuffle (2) = 10, meta 16 bits -> 0xB21A1001
// cd_values[5]: Bitshuffle (2) runs last
unsigned int cd_values[7] = { 0xB21A1001, 0, 0, 0, 5, 2, 1 };
H5Pset_filter(plist_id, 32026, H5Z_FLAG_MANDATORY, 7, cd_values);

Lists in other forms

The plugin reads cd_values[0] to tell what kind of list it was handed, both from your H5Pset_filter() call and from a creation property list copied from another dataset (as h5repack and H5Dget_create_plist() hand them on), and converts each to the layout above:

  • 0: the form earlier versions of hdf5lib documented, still accepted: { 0, 0, 0, 0, level, bitmask, codec, meta }, with the pre-filter bitmask in cd_values[5] and the meta value as an optional 8th value. The example above in this form is { 0, 0, 0, 0, 5, 10, 1, 16 }, and it stores exactly the same list. Here cd_values[5] is still the bitmask, not a filter code. The option tuples hdf5plugin’s Blosc2() builds also start with 0, so they are read this way too, and two of its codes mean something else: 3 (its DELTA) is shuffle + bitshuffle, so bitshuffle, and 4 (its TRUNC_PREC) is delta. Passing no values at all also lands here: level 5, shuffle, BloscLZ.
  • 1: the reference filter’s own lists, such as a creation property list copied from a dataset h5py wrote. cd_values[5] is one filter code (0 none, 1 shuffle, 2 bitshuffle, 3 delta, 4 trunc-prec); there is no meta value, so trunc-prec fails H5Dcreate2() on native floats (it has no precision to keep) and NDLZ uses 4 x 4 cells. Any other code fails H5Dcreate2().
  • 2: lists stored by hdf5lib 2.1.1.0 to 2.2.0.0 (and development builds of 2.2.0.1): the bitmask in the low byte of cd_values[5], and the meta value in its next byte (lists of 7 values) or after the chunk shape.
  • 0xB2...: the layout above. A layout version other than 1 fails H5Dcreate2().

Any other cd_values[0] fails H5Dcreate2(). When the plugin compresses chunks for a dataset already in a file, such as one being appended to, it reads the stored list the same way: a dataset an earlier hdf5lib wrote keeps the settings it recorded, and one another implementation wrote gets the single pre-filter its cd_values[5] names, as the reference filter would run it. It refuses to compress with a layout version it does not know. Reading does not depend on any of these settings, because every Blosc2 chunk records its own pre-filters, codec and parameters.
